items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I went into this one session with Butch Miles, the drummer, and this was for Harry Lim, the Famous Door Records guy.

ctx.x: Bass players seem to be at the mercy of the sound people, more than anybody.

Man, I’ve got stories you know. I went into this one session with Butch Miles, the drummer, and this was for Harry Lim, the Famous Door Records guy. And they had a young pony-tailed engineer there, and I had just gotten my new Underwood pick-up, which is good for live situations you know. At the time it seemed, I can play louder now, it’s great. I get in there and we hook it up and we’ve got a direct sound on the thing and we do a little test track, and I said that’s terrible. I mean the pick-up, it’s a good…
matter, don’t you have one? I have one you can use mine.” And the guy says, “No, no, no, no. That sound that you just got? That’s what we want, we’re going to stay with it.
